objective: Review the definition-only native Verilator invocation boundary after the scoped direct command-path sidecar execution run, decide whether a later non-executing fixture may be implemented, and keep this review from claiming native option support, direct Verilator command execution, new sidecar execution, compare execution, timing, speedup, arbitrary filelist support, automatic GPU allocation, runtime/ABI change, or raw full-state equality.

review_decision.reason: The boundary is narrow enough to move to a non-executing fixture because it starts from a real Verilator-facing command with the expanded --sim-accel sidecar-gpu state/step spelling, requires explicit reviewed sidecar context before any sidecar stage can run, preserves ordinary Verilator files and filelists as inputs, and explicitly denies runtime authority to wrapper execution, fixture metadata, materialized stage-plan metadata, and generated command text.
review_decision.weakest_point: The boundary still names a future real Verilator invocation, but no later implementation has executed such an invocation yet. A direct-looking command, fixture metadata, materialized stage-plan metadata, or generated command text can therefore be over-read as runtime authority. The next implementation must remain non-executing metadata validation only and must not call Verilator, sidecar stages, compare, timing, allocation, runtime/ABI code, or source-closure inference.

the minimum future invocation form begins with a Verilator-facing command and uses the expanded --sim-accel spelling

target, mode, template or registry entry, and source gate or manifest remain explicit sidecar context
wrapper execution, direct fixture metadata, materialized stage-plan metadata, and generated command text are not promoted to runtime authority
dry-run, preview, execution, and timing modes remain separate before implementation
filelists and source files remain preserved Verilator inputs rather than inferred dependency closure
